 Week 12: SDSU at Southern Illinois - What I'm watching
 Jackrabbits look to strengthen playoff position in regular season road finale
 SDSU captains await the coin toss prior to their 2026 season opener against Stetson on Aug. 29 at Dana J. Dykhouse Stadium in Brookings. Jenn Kenyon/Sioux Falls Live 
 By 
 Matt Zimmer

 CARBONDALE, Ill. — No, I didn't make the trip for this one, and I'm glad I didn't, as I'd probably be stranded in an airport somewhere. Luckily, the Jackrabbits' charter took off before every airplane in the country was grounded, so No. 4 South Dakota State's game against Southern Illinois is on as scheduled, Saturday at 1 p.m.
 Here's what I'll be keeping an eye on from afar.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Can the Jacks repeat last week's road excellence? 
Northern Iowa was 4-0 at home going into last week's game against the Jacks, but suggestions that the Panthers could actually win the game felt kind of forced. 
Still, SDSU wasn't going to take any chances after their loss at UND, and Dan Jackson's messaging both in the aftermath of that loss in the weeks since has clearly resonated. 
They talked about the motivations UNI would take into the game, and SIU's in a similar spot this week. At 5-5, the Salukis aren't quite out of the playoff hunt yet. Win this and win next week and maybe they're in at 7-5. 
It's Senior Day, their final home game, probably the final home game for SIU QB DJ Williams, an all-time great Saluki.
The Jacks are taking all of that into account. SIU shouldn't be able to catch them off guard.
 What will DJ Williams have in store for the Jacks? 
A Walter Payton finalist last year, Williams got hurt early in the season and while he missed only one game he's clearly been playing hurt. He's still been effective, but not as explosive as he was a year ago. Jackson said Williams looks closer to 100 percent healthy now, and if that's true he'll give the Salukis a much better chance at the upset.
Of course, the Jacks have already slowed down the best running QB in the league in Beau Brungard. If SDSU's defense stays assignment sound they should be fine, but playing in his final home game it's always possible Williams will do something special.
 Can the passing game build on its success? 
The Jacks have been pretty efficient through the air during their three-game winning streak, and in the win over UNI they showed some explosiveness, hitting some downfield shots that forced the Panther defense to back off, opening running lanes for Josiah Johnson and James Basinger.
 That's something the Jacks should look to keep building on. Let's see more explosives. More deep shots. More Lofton O'Groske. More Brayden Delahoyde.
 Yes, just getting the 'W' is the most important thing, but if SDSU can consisently connect deep down the field it's only going to build their confidence as an offense and give opposing defenses that much more to worry about.
